title: Only White Pieces??
transcript: I'm a 1700 rated player and my opponent is Zach Ainsley, a currently unrated bodybuilder. And we [music] are playing on a very unique board where every square and every piece is completely white, which means that it's up to us to remember which [music] pieces are whose to avoid confusion. I eventually managed to win a pawn in the center thanks to a tactic, but Zach has only been playing chess for about two years [music] and earlier that day he had drawn David Howell. Yes, Grandmaster David Howell. Once we're deep in a middle game, we start to forget which pieces are whose and Zach tries to push my pawn in this position. Wait, I think that's my pawn. >> Is that your pawn? Oh my this game, I swear I don't >> [laughter] >> Yeah, it was like, "Oh my god, he's a genius." And it doesn't take too long for me to make the same mistake. Isn't that my pawn? I don't know. No, is it? Oh no. >> No, it's not. Is it not? I don't think so. Oh, we're going to have to check. Well, it's mine now. Okay. >> [laughter] >> I eventually managed to win this game and so we agreed to play a rematch. This time I play as black and I decide to go for a French defense. But after getting distracted by Dennis beating Hikaru, we forget where our pieces [music] are placed. Right. >> [laughter] >> Yeah. That's yours. That's yours. Yes, yes. But then something crazy happens. I attack the bishop of Zach and he just ignores the threat and moves the knight, a brilliant move that I ignore like a fool and allow him to fork my king and queen. Damn it. There's simply nothing I can do and so I end up resigning the game. Yeah, two years, guys.
